overview: S1B is clientbound mount and leash state, and the corpus shows three real consumers: Grim converts the 1.8 attach into its 1.9+ mount format inside PacketEntityReplication, Artemis folds the player's attach into the prediction vehicle under a transaction confirmation, and Intave registers an AttachEntityReader plus an entity-tracker hook. The remaining hits are noise: NCP's attach terms are listener and block-attachment bookkeeping, Argus's CheckAttachedModules is its own client-module report channel, and Negativity, FlopAC and Artemis contribute constants and wrappers. The flagging side of vehicle exploits stays on the inbound C03 stream; these checks exist to keep the simulated vehicle state honest.

checks.name: Attach replication (Grim)
checks.purpose: Mirror the server's mount state into the compensated entity tracker so movement and vehicle checks know what the player and tracked entities are riding.
checks.how_it_works: PacketEntityReplication parses WrapperPlayServerAttachEntity on the ATTACH_ENTITY send, ignores it on 1.9+ servers (replaced by SET_PASSENGERS), and for non-leash attaches converts the 1.8 format into handleMountVehicle: vehicleId -1 dismounts using the stored legacyPointEightMountedUpon, otherwise the mount pair is recorded. An attach naming an untracked entity logs a warning because the client itself would ignore it. SetbackTeleportUtil sends the matching detach during teleport setbacks so a player cannot re-enter a vehicle to keep a cheat active.
checks.detects: Nothing directly: state replication. It removes mount-state desync as a variable when movement checks evaluate vehicle motion, and the setback-time detach closes the vehicle-reentry bypass during lag-backs.
checks.variations: Grim SetbackTeleportUtil (line 246) emits the detach itself on the 1.8 wire path during setbacks. No other anticheat mirrors attach state into a simulation.

checks.name: Vehicle prediction sync (Artemis)
checks.purpose: Apply the player's attach and detach to the prediction engine under a transaction confirmation so movement emulation knows when the player rides a vehicle.
checks.how_it_works: MiscellaneousPreProcessor matches GPacketPlayServerEntityAttach: when the attach targets the player's own entity id, it registers a confirmFunctionAndTick on the TRANSACTION confirmation; at pre() the prediction vehicle is set from the vehicle id through NMS, and a null vehicle triggers resetMotion so the emulator stops attributing vehicle physics to the player.
checks.detects: Nothing directly: state sync. It feeds EmulatorPreProcessor's vehicle-aware movement simulation, which is what keeps vehicle-related motion flags accurate.
checks.variations: Kauri PacketHandler (line 431) wraps the same packet on the send side. Intave tracks attach state through EntityTracker.sendAttachEntityPacket (line 120) in addition to its reader. FlopAC's WrappedOutAttachEntity and Artemis's own GPacketPlayServerEntityAttach are wrappers; Negativity's ATTACH_ENTITY constant is a registration.

checks.name: Attach reader (Intave)
checks.purpose: Expose the attach packet's two int fields (entity id, vehicle id) to the substitution pipeline so entity filters can rewrite or drop attach packets.
checks.how_it_works: AttachEntityReader extends AbstractPacketReader and implements EntityIterable: entityId() and vehicleId() read the two ints, and the SubstitutionIterator allows filters to write either field back into the packet (slot 1 rewrites the entity id, slot 2 the vehicle id). It is registered in PacketReaders as ATTACH_ENTITY.
checks.detects: Nothing directly: a packet reader. It is the intake point for Intave's entity substitution and filtering, which feed the entity tracker that movement checks consult.
checks.variations: Intave's EntityTracker also subscribes to the attach packet directly, and firework-rocket attach tracking in MovementMetadata is a separate 1.9+ mechanism. NCP's attach corpus hits are logger and listener bookkeeping, and Argus's CheckAttachedModules is its own client-module report channel; neither reads S1B.
